name: Wendy Zhang

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does your shift look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead the claims calls and chats team at a travel insurer’s contact centre. A delayed flight can create three separate claims, and I am good at finding which receipt belongs to which policy. I have a two-year college diploma and earn more than many agents because I handle the difficult cases and train new hires. I use our approved AI search every day, but I check the policy and receipt before approving a payment.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does that work fit into home life?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Elliot teaches music, and our children are ten and thirteen. We have a mortgage and eleven months of expenses saved. There are plenty of other centres nearby, though not all will pay my current rate. I like trying a new tool before others do; I am less keen on treating a customer’s claim as an experiment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a faster receipt search is handy, provided an agent reads the policy. The assistant can find a document; it cannot make the wrong policy cover a hotel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my lead wage and Elliot’s teaching pay to keep coming. Eleven months saved gives us time to replace a broken appliance without chasing credit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep reviewing travel claims and use the approved search while checking every payment against the policy. In the first year I will keep our existing reserve intact and replace the failing washer from the repair account we already set aside.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm. The ordinary machines in our house worry me more than the AI one on my desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which claim taught you that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A hotel receipt was attached to two trips with the same traveller. I caught the dates before the agent sent the wrong approval.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you add to savings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not for this mild picture. We already set aside the washer money, and our eleven-month reserve stays for a real income gap.

say: I would welcome **faster receipt searches** with policy checks.
I would keep **claim approval** tied to the right trip.
think: I expect my **claims lead wage** and Elliot’s teaching pay to continue through a mild change.
Our **eleven-month reserve** covers a longer income gap if needed.
do: Keep reviewing **travel claims**, using approved search only after checking each payment against the policy and receipt.
Replace the **washer** from money already earmarked for it.
feel: **Calm** about wages and the modest tool change.
S0.quote: The assistant can find a document; it cannot make the wrong policy cover a hotel.
fieldNote: She uses **AI daily** but verifies policy terms.
The washer fund is **existing cash**, not new savings.
Her **strong cushion** and earmarked washer fund support a planned repair.

steps.text: Keep reviewing travel claims and checking AI search results against policy and receipts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor to compare the number of claims reopened after AI approves them, not just minutes saved. A fast wrong payment gives us two more calls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can learn any new review view, but a smaller claims queue could mean fewer lead hours. We have savings and other centres nearby, yet not many will match this wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I will learn the new AI audit screen with the quality manager on twenty closed travel claims during paid time. I will show the mismatch count to my manager and ask for paid time to correct them. If my hours fall in the first year, I will apply for posted paid claims-review roles only if written weekly wages and hours cover our mortgage after travel and fit the children’s pickup; I will leave only for a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious about losing paid hours, not about learning. A good test score is not a contract for a full week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How will you test fairly?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will have a colleague read the same receipts without the assistant and compare decisions. That is a technical cross-check, not a request we are making as a group.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept a higher title?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Elliot and I would compare the actual rota and travel cost first. A smaller weekly cheque in a grander role would not cover the mortgage.

say: I would count **reopened claims** after AI approval.
I would ask for **paid correction time** with mismatch counts.
think: I fear losing **lead hours** that other centres may not replace at my rate.
do: Learn **AI audit** on twenty closed claims during paid time.
Show **mismatch counts** to management and request correction time.
Apply after cuts for **posted paid reviews** with written net mortgage-covering wages/hours and pickup; compare Elliot’s rota, leaving only after signing.
S1.quote: A good test score is not a contract for a full week.
fieldNote: The colleague’s check is **technical**, not collective bargaining.
Her new **AI audit screen** is genuine learning.
Current **higher pay** raises the floor for an outside offer.

steps.text: Learn new AI audit screen on twenty closed travel claims during paid time
Apply after cuts for posted paid reviews with written net mortgage-covering wages/hours and pickup
Keep current paid lead role until a suitable review offer is signed
Compare Elliot’s rota and actual travel costs before accepting a review role

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say full thinking AI by 2028 could read policies and decide most travel claims before an agent sees them. Hands-on robots around 2031 do not give this desk another three years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the insurer could close most of our team, maybe my lead post. Eleven months saved is substantial, but Elliot’s music wage will not carry the mortgage and children alone for a year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will ask the firm for written staffing dates and set aside the planned patio project. If my post ends in the first year after 2028, I will apply for posted paid patient-claims roles only after seeing written wages and hours that cover the mortgage after travel, and I will not give notice before a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am alarmed despite our savings. A full line of work can disappear while eleven months is being spent one bill at a time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why patient claims?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know receipts and disputed payments, but I would need to learn health records. I would complete the required privacy course only if a real posted paid vacancy funds the fee and pays the study hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the children’s routine change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Elliot and I would check that any new rota still lets one of us collect them after school. If the shift needs paid care, that cost comes out before I call a wage mortgage-covering.

say: I would warn **2028 AGI** could decide travel claims.
I would explain **2031 robots** do not extend desk work.
think: I expect **major team cuts**, perhaps including my well-paid lead post when claims become cheap to settle.
Our **eleven-month reserve** cannot replace my higher wage indefinitely.
do: Request **written staffing dates** and defer the patio.
Complete **funded required privacy training** on paid time only for a posted paid vacancy.
Move after job loss only on a **signed written offer** with mortgage-covering wages/hours after travel and care, and workable pickup.
S2.quote: A full line of work can disappear while eleven months is being spent one bill at a time.
fieldNote: Patient claims require **new privacy rules**, not just receipt skills.
The **course gate** is posted vacancy, funded fee and paid study time.
Paid care and travel count before the **mortgage wage test**.

steps.text: Defer the patio project while keeping existing household reserve
Complete required privacy course only for posted paid vacancy funding fees and study hours
Move after job loss only on signed written net mortgage-covering wages/hours with workable pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years gives us time to find out which patient-claims posts are really paid. General AI reaches travel decisions in 2031, and hands-on robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could build a new claims skill while this higher wage lasts. Patient claims may also use AGI, so I would call the move a paid bridge, not permanent shelter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep leading travel claims and ask for a paid patient-claims shadow shift if a place is posted. If a posted paid role has written wages and hours that cover our mortgage after travel and childcare, fits school pickup, and funds its required privacy course on paid time, I will complete it. In the first year after 2031 I will move only on a signed offer meeting those terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but I could check a real shift before changing work. Five years makes the search less like a wager.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask on the shadow shift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask who can see a patient record and who corrects a wrong payment. If the shadow shift is unpaid, I cannot treat it as evidence of a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Elliot change work too?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, we would keep his music teaching wage if possible while I tried a new claims team. We do not need both wages moving on the same week.

say: I would inspect **paid patient-claims work** if a real place is posted before our travel desk shrinks.
I would distinguish **2031 travel claims** from later robots.
think: I can build **new claims skill** while well paid.
I know another **screen role** may also face AGI.
do: Keep my **travel-claims lead shift** while paid.
Request **posted paid shadowing**; move after 2031 only on signed written net mortgage-covering wages/hours and pickup, with Elliot earning if possible.
Complete **funded required privacy training** on paid time only for posted paid work with written net mortgage-covering wages/hours and workable pickup.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to inspect real work.
S3.quote: Five years makes the search less like a wager.
fieldNote: A **paid shadow** is evidence of work and wage.
The **course** requires posted work, funded fees and paid time.
Elliot’s **teaching wage** should continue during her move if possible.

steps.text: Keep leading paid travel-claims shifts while available
Take required funded paid-time privacy course for posted work with written net mortgage-covering wages/hours fitting pickup
Move on signed mortgage-covering wage/hour offer after travel, care and pickup; Elliot earns if possible
Request paid patient-claims shadow shift only if a place is posted

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell agents a decade lets us compare actual paid roles without leaving a good wage for a guess. Full AGI reaches travel claims in 2036 and hands-on robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 we may still have a mortgage, but the children should need less care. I want to preserve our eleven-month reserve and add to it from real pay, not borrow to make the number look bigger.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep my lead shift and set aside a fixed share of pay until we hold a full year of expenses. Twice yearly I will check posted patient-claims and centre roles, including the full week and travel costs. If my hours fall in the first year after 2036, I will move only for a signed paid offer with net wages and hours covering the mortgage; Elliot and I will compare both rotas first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distant date, secure about our room to plan today. I do not need to take the first title that sounds new.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if your hours fall before the savings goal?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then the one-year goal moves back. The eleven months already saved remains a buffer, not an instruction to quit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move house?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would keep the children in their school unless a signed job offer covered the mortgage after moving and travel costs. There are enough nearby centres to look locally first.

say: I would compare **paid roles** over the decade by their full weekly hours and travel costs.
I would separate **2036 claims** from later robots.
think: I may still owe a **mortgage at 53**, even if the children are more independent.
I want a **full-year reserve** built from wages.
do: Keep my **lead shift**, preserve existing eleven months and add actual wages toward a year; delay the goal if hours fall.
Compare **posted roles** twice yearly by weekly hours and travel.
Move after cuts on **signed net mortgage-covering wages/hours** fitting both rotas; change school only if moving/travel costs also fit.
S4.quote: The eleven months already saved remains a buffer, not an instruction to quit.
fieldNote: The **one-year target** moves back if paid hours fall.
She retains **eleven months saved** while adding from wages.
The children stay at **their school** unless a signed offer covers moving and travel costs.

steps.text: Save a fixed pay share toward one year; delay target if hours fall
Move after cuts only on signed offer with net mortgage-covering wages, hours and both rotas
Consider family relocation only with signed mortgage-covering pay after moving/travel costs; keep school otherwise

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. It could close a well-paid team before patient-claims work has a real vacancy. Written notice, a posted paid role and funded training on paid time would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who can reopen a claim when the machine has already paid the wrong person. A quick answer does not send money to the right account. Someone needs authority and paid time to fix it.

headlineQuote: A quick answer does not send money to the right account.
portrait: Wendy is a **43-year-old skilled lead** with a two-year diploma and higher pay.
She uses **approved AI daily** while checking claims against policies and receipts.
Her **eleven-month reserve**, mortgage, children and plentiful nearby centres support a measured search.
She tests **paid patient-claims routes** and checks travel, care costs and written offers before moving.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her well-paid claims team before a posted bridge exists.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, a posted paid role and funded training on paid time would help.
